intro: Object detectors often predict several boxes for one object. Greedy suppression keeps confident boxes while removing later boxes whose overlap is too large.
task: Trace greedy box selection and explain how score order, exact ties, and threshold equality change retained detections.
requirements: boxes is a finite (N,4) matrix of continuous [xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax] coordinates with nonnegative side lengths; scores is a length-N real vector; 0<=threshold<=1.
Consider boxes by descending score, breaking ties by lower original index. Keep a box unless its IoU with an already-kept box is strictly greater than threshold.
Return kept original indices as a Python list in selection order. IoU for zero union is 0. This is class-agnostic greedy NMS; no score cutoff or maximum count is applied.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Sort once with an explicit tie rule
hints.body: Confidence determines the greedy order; original index resolves exact ties.

hints.title: Compare only against retained boxes
hints.body: A discarded box must not suppress another candidate later.

explanation: Greedy NMS is order-dependent: a high-confidence box is retained first and can suppress lower-ranked alternatives. The algorithm does not optimize a global set objective.
Only overlaps strictly above the threshold are suppressed. That boundary and the tie policy make deterministic evaluation possible across implementations.
